paragraphs.source_en: To this distressful emblem of a great distress that had long been growing worse, and was not at its worst, a woman was kneeling. She turned her head as the carriage came up to her, rose quickly, and presented herself at the carriage-door.

units.source_en: To this distressful emblem of a great distress that had long been growing worse, and was not at its worst, a woman was kneeling.
She turned her head as the carriage came up to her, rose quickly, and presented herself at the carriage-door.

paragraphs.source_en: “It is you, Monseigneur! Monseigneur, a petition.”
With an exclamation of impatience, but with his unchangeable face, Monseigneur looked out.

units.source_en: With an exclamation of impatience, but with his unchangeable face, Monseigneur looked out.

paragraphs.source_en: “How, then! What is it? Always petitions!”
“Monseigneur. For the love of the great God! My husband, the forester.”

paragraphs.source_en: “What of your husband, the forester? Always the same with you people. He cannot pay something?”

paragraphs.source_en: She looked an old woman, but was young. Her manner was one of passionate grief; by turns she clasped her veinous and knotted hands together with wild energy, and laid one of them on the carriage-door—tenderly, caressingly, as if it had been a human breast, and could be expected to feel the appealing touch.

paragraphs.source_en: “Monseigneur, hear me! Monseigneur, hear my petition! My husband died of want; so many die of want; so many more will die of want.”

units.source_en: My husband died of want; so many die of want; so many more will die of want.”

paragraphs.source_en: “Monseigneur, the good God knows; but I don’t ask it. My petition is, that a morsel of stone or wood, with my husband’s name, may be placed over him to show where he lies. Otherwise, the place will be quickly forgotten, it will never be found when I am dead of the same malady, I shall be laid under some other heap of poor grass. Monseigneur, they are so many, they increase so fast, there is so much want. Monseigneur! Monseigneur!”

paragraphs.source_en: The valet had put her away from the door, the carriage had broken into a brisk trot, the postilions had quickened the pace, she was left far behind, and Monseigneur, again escorted by the Furies, was rapidly diminishing the league or two of distance that remained between him and his chateau.
